country.name: United Arab Emirates
country.coastline: Arabian Gulf (west coast) and Gulf of Oman (east coast, outside the Strait of Hormuz)
country.summary: The UAE is the Gulf's dominant transhipment and re-export hub, anchored by DP World's Jebel Ali (15.5m TEU in 2024, 19.4m TEU capacity) and AD Ports Group's Khalifa Port (group throughput 7.7m TEU in 2025), with Gulftainer's Khor Fakkan and the Port of Fujairah providing the only deep-sea gateways on the Gulf of Oman side. The 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis (closure from 28 February 2026) cut Jebel Ali volumes by 90% in Q2 2026 and triggered a structural pivot to the east coast: DP World signed a 50-year concession for two new Fujairah terminals (Al Rugaylat and Dibba, July 2026), Gulftainer launched a US$2bn plan to lift Khor Fakkan to 10m TEU, and Etihad Rail's 900 km freight network became the domestic landbridge from Fujairah/Khalifa Port to the Gulf coast. Free zones (JAFZA, KEZAD, Dubai South, DMCC, RAKEZ, Hamriyah, SAIF) host tens of thousands of trading and manufacturing firms, while road crossings to Saudi Arabia (Al Ghuweifat) and Oman (Hatta, Khatmat Malaha, Mezyad) carry the Gulf's land trade and were heavily congested during the 2026 crisis.

ports.name: Jebel Ali Port
ports.concession: DP World flagship, wholly owned and operated; no third-party concession (DP World is majority-owned by Dubai World / Port & Free Zone World)
ports.capacity: 19.4m TEU/year across 4 container terminals (T1–T4); 27 berths, c.5,000 m quay, 101 quay cranes; 75,000 CEU vehicle storage after Aug 2025 ro-ro expansion (800 m ro-ro quay)
ports.throughput: 15.5m TEU (2024, 9th in Lloyd's List Top 100); O&D volumes +9% in 2025; breakbulk 5.67m t (2025); 1.5m vehicles across Dubai terminals (2025). H1 2026: 3.1m TEU (−59.5% YoY), Q2 2026: 374,000 TEU (−90.1% YoY) due to Hormuz closure
ports.projects: Jebel Ali expansion is a named priority in DP World's ~US$3bn 2026 capex (Feb 2026); Aug 2025 vehicle-capacity expansion (+13,000 CEU, 2.6m sq ft yard, 800 m ro-ro quay); integration with new Fujairah terminals via DP World inland network (Fujairah terminals due 24–30 months from July 2026, c.2028)
ports.notes: DP WORLD FLAGSHIP ASSET. Hormuz closure from 28 Feb 2026 collapsed vessel calls; March 2026 debris from an intercepted Iranian missile/drone caused a berth fire and temporary suspension but no lasting infrastructure damage; port 'remains fully operational'. Splash247 estimated the slump costs DP World ~US$100m/month; DP World H1 2026 profit −39.1% to US$585m. Connected to JAFZA, Al Maktoum Airport (Dubai Logistics Corridor) and an Etihad Rail freight terminal.

ports.name: Mina Rashid (Port Rashid)
ports.operator: DP World (cargo/ro-ro and cruise terminals); P&O Marinas (DP World) for marina
ports.capacity: Cargo & ro-ro terminal: 15 berths, 2,757 m quay, 10.5 m draft; coastal terminal: 5 berths, 900 m quay, 5 m draft; Hamdan bin Mohammed Cruise Terminal handles 7 mega-cruise vessels / 27,000 passengers simultaneously
ports.throughput: c.1m cruise passengers/year (DP World, current); cargo tonnage n/a
ports.notes: DP WORLD ASSET. Dubai's original port; container operations moved to Jebel Ali in 2008 and Mina Rashid is now the Middle East's leading cruise homeport (World Travel Awards, 15 consecutive years) with break-bulk, ro-ro, coastal/dhow and yacht-marina business.

ports.name: Khalifa Port
ports.operator: AD Ports Group (landlord); terminals: Abu Dhabi Terminals (ADT), CSP Abu Dhabi (COSCO Shipping Ports), CMA Terminals Khalifa Port (CMA CGM 70% / AD Ports 30%), Khalifa Port Logistics, Abu Dhabi Maritime
ports.concession: ADT container terminal 30-year concession to 2042; CSP Abu Dhabi concession with COSCO Shipping Ports (opened 2018); CMA Terminals JV (CMA CGM 70%/AD Ports 30%) opened Dec 2024
ports.capacity: Container capacity to reach 10.5m TEU/year after CMA Terminals expansion (2028); CSP Abu Dhabi 2.5m TEU, 1,200 m quay, 18.5 m draft, 3 berths, 11 STS cranes; CMA Terminals 1.8m TEU (to 2.7m TEU)
ports.throughput: AD Ports Group total 7.7m TEU (2025, +23%); CMA Terminals Khalifa Port 1.3m TEU in first full year (2025, 74% utilisation); general cargo c.60m t group-wide (2025)
ports.projects: CMA Terminals expansion +0.9m TEU to 2.7m TEU, AED 420m (US$115m), completion early 2028 (signed Nov 2025); LNG/LPG terminal hubs >AED 30bn announced 2025; bonded Etihad Rail corridor Khalifa Port–Fujairah (pilot late 2025)
ports.notes: COMPETITOR TO JEBEL ALI. Semi-automated terminal with direct Etihad Rail freight terminal and KEZAD hinterland. COSCO and CMA CGM concessions make it the main carrier-backed alternative in the UAE. 2012 Phase 1 masterplan targeted 15m TEU by 2030.

ports.name: Zayed Port (Mina Zayed)
ports.capacity: 21 berths, 3,450 m quay, 13–14 m depth alongside, 5.3 km2 area; handles up to 10 ocean-going vessels simultaneously; general cargo capacity 7.5m FT (AD Ports)
ports.throughput: n/a (part of AD Ports Group c.60m t general cargo, 2025)
ports.projects: Abu Dhabi Cruise Terminal development; port area being progressively redeveloped as container handling moved to Khalifa Port
ports.notes: Abu Dhabi's main gateway for bulk, break-bulk and general cargo, plus cruise hub; 5 minutes from E11 highway in downtown Abu Dhabi.

ports.name: Khor Fakkan (Khorfakkan Container Terminal)
ports.operator: Gulftainer (Crescent Enterprises) under Sharjah Ports Authority
ports.concession: Gulftainer has managed the terminal since 1976 for the Government of Sharjah; term n/a
ports.capacity: Being raised from 3.5m to 5m TEU/year (mid-2026); 6 deep-sea berths, 18 STS cranes (post- and super-post-Panamax), 450,000 m2 yard
ports.throughput: Weekly throughput rose from c.8,000 TEU pre-crisis to c.65,000 TEU (July 2026); truck traffic from c.100 to 7,000/day; annual figure n/a
ports.projects: Gulftainer US$2bn expansion (announced July 2026): 5m TEU within 3 months, 7m TEU in 24 months, >10m TEU in 36 months; new berth; Al Dhaid dry port (1.5m TEU) and Sajaa logistics park, 2.3m TEU inland capacity; agreement to connect Khor Fakkan to Etihad Rail
ports.notes: COMPETITOR (Gulftainer). Only major container port outside Hormuz before DP World's Fujairah build; shifted from transhipment to UAE gateway role in 2026. Gulftainer CEO claims ability to absorb 80–90% of UAE container demand if Hormuz shuts again; GT Maritime feeder fleet >10,000 boxes/week. Congestion/waiting times doubled Aug 2026 (nautica-shipping).

ports.name: Port of Fujairah
ports.operator: Fujairah Ports Authority (Government of Fujairah); Fujairah Oil Tanker Terminals (FOTT) for liquid bulk; Vopak Horizon, ADNOC and others in FOIZ
ports.concession: Government port; FOTT operates oil berths; DP World 50-year concession (July 2026) for new Al Rugaylat and Dibba terminals
ports.capacity: FOTT: 9 main or 14 wing berths (up to 200,000 dwt) plus VLCC jetty (330,000 dwt, since 2016); c.18m m3 crude/product storage in FOIZ; Habshan–Fujairah pipeline delivers 1.5m bpd
ports.throughput: 7.4m m3 marine fuel bunkers (2025, 4th globally); >1.7m bpd crude and products exported (2025/26); container volumes n/a
ports.projects: DP World Al Rugaylat container/multipurpose terminal (2.5m TEU, 1.7m t general cargo, 190,000 CEU) and Dibba general-cargo terminal (3.6m t), 50-year concession, 24–30 months build from July 2026; ADNOC underground crude storage cavern (three crude grades); Etihad Rail freight terminal and bonded rail corridor to Khalifa Port
ports.notes: DP WORLD ENTRY (July 2026). World's top-4 bunkering hub and the UAE's Hormuz-bypass crude outlet; drone strikes on 14–15 March 2026 disrupted loadings. New terminals lift DP World UAE capacity from 19.4m to c.22m TEU; Fujairah waiting times doubled in Aug 2026 amid Hormuz stalemate.

ports.name: Port Khalid (Sharjah Container Terminal)
ports.operator: Gulftainer (Sharjah Container Terminal) under Sharjah Ports Authority
ports.projects: Sharjah ports upgrade programme (MEED); Gulftainer US$2bn Sharjah strategy (2026) including Sharjah Dry Port and Sajaa Dry Port
ports.notes: COMPETITOR (Gulftainer). Sharjah's city-centre multipurpose/container port on the Gulf side; Gulftainer's original terminal. Limited recent public volume data.

ports.name: Hamriyah Port
ports.operator: Hamriyah Free Zone Authority (port); Gulftainer historically operated the container facility
ports.capacity: 14 m deep outer port and 7 m inner harbour (HFZA); liquid bulk, general cargo, container
ports.notes: Port-linked to the 24 km2 Hamriyah Free Zone; oil & gas services, petrochemical storage and steel/industrial cargo. Not to be confused with DP World's Mina Al Hamriya in Dubai (expanded 2024).

ports.name: Saqr Port
ports.operator: RAK Ports (Government of Ras Al Khaimah); Stevin Rock is the anchor quarry exporter
ports.capacity: RAK Ports operates c.60 berths across Saqr Port, RAK Port, Al Jazeera Port and RAK Maritime City (2025); Saqr is the Middle East's largest bulk (aggregates/cement/clinker) port
ports.throughput: n/a (tonnage not published in accessed sources)
ports.projects: Saqr 2.0 greenfield port and free zone: 72 berths in phase 1, 17–18 m depth, 5m m2 free-zone land (to 14m m2), liquid bulk/project cargo/ship repair/recycling; phase 1 operational by 2027 (RAK Ports, 2025)
ports.notes: Main outlet for Stevin Rock/RAK quarries supplying aggregates across the Gulf; Etihad Rail's busiest freight stations include Ras Al Khaimah (aggregate trains). Deep-water Saqr 2.0 would be the region's deepest port.

zones.name: Jebel Ali Free Zone (JAFZA)
zones.authority: DP World (Jafza / Ports, Customs and Free Zone Corporation)
zones.area: n/a (c.57 km2 widely cited; not confirmed in accessed sources)
zones.incentives: 100% foreign ownership, 0% customs duty within zone, corporate tax relief for qualifying free-zone income, full repatriation of capital and profits
zones.tenants: >11,000 companies; US$190bn trade in 12 months to May 2025 (+15%); c.75% of Dubai's FDI in manufacturing, trade and transport
zones.projects: Integration with Dubai Logistics Corridor (Jebel Ali–Dubai South–Al Maktoum airport); DP World to link new Fujairah terminals to Jafza via inland network (2026)
zones.notes: DP WORLD ASSET; Middle East's first free zone, contiguous with Jebel Ali Port.

zones.name: Khalifa Economic Zones Abu Dhabi (KEZAD, formerly KIZAD)
zones.area: >550 km2 across 12 economic zones, of which 100 km2 free zone
zones.incentives: Choice of free-zone or domestic (onshore) jurisdiction; 100% foreign ownership in free zone; customs-bonded status; long-term land leases; direct Khalifa Port and Etihad Rail access
zones.tenants: >2,300 clients (>400 free-zone); 540,000+ m2 warehouses; 164,000+ jobs; hosts EGA aluminium smelter
zones.projects: KEZAD Business District announced June 2025; ongoing expansion of warehousing and staff accommodation; Etihad Rail freight terminal at ICAD/Khalifa Port
zones.notes: COMPETITOR hinterland (AD Ports Group); claims 55% of UAE industrial area.

zones.name: Dubai South (Dubai World Central) – Logistics District
zones.authority: Dubai South (Government of Dubai) / Dubai Aviation City Corporation
zones.area: c.145 km2 master development (Dubai South); logistics district n/a
zones.incentives: Free-zone licensing, bonded Dubai Logistics Corridor linking Jebel Ali Port to Al Maktoum airport (sea–air in hours), 100% foreign ownership
zones.tenants: >4,200 operating businesses (2025), 653 new companies in 2025 (+65% licences)
zones.projects: AED 128bn Al Maktoum International Airport expansion: 260m passengers and 12m t cargo ultimate capacity, five runways, first phase c.150m passengers (announced 2024)
zones.notes: Adjacent to DP World's Jebel Ali; core of the Dubai Logistics Corridor.

zones.name: Dubai Multi Commodities Centre (DMCC)
zones.incentives: 100% foreign ownership, 0% personal income tax, free-zone corporate-tax regime, commodity exchanges (DGCX, Dubai Diamond Exchange)
zones.notes: Trading (not port-side) zone; world's third-largest diamond trading hub. Relevant for commodity-flow origination rather than physical logistics.

zones.name: Dubai Industrial City
zones.incentives: Onshore (non-free-zone) industrial land and warehouses with dual licensing options; proximity to Jebel Ali and Al Maktoum airport
zones.tenants: n/a (six sector zones; >20 companies in F&B zone per Wikipedia)
zones.projects: Hosts one of Etihad Rail's seven freight terminals
zones.notes: Etihad Rail freight terminal makes it Dubai's inland rail-served industrial hub.

zones.name: Hamriyah Free Zone
zones.authority: Hamriyah Free Zone Authority (Government of Sharjah)
zones.incentives: 100% foreign ownership, 100% repatriation, no import/export duties within zone, own 14 m deep port
zones.notes: Largest industrial free zone in Sharjah; integral port.

zones.name: Sharjah Airport International Free Zone (SAIF Zone)
zones.incentives: 100% foreign ownership, tax exemptions, licence in as little as one hour (SAIF Zone)
zones.notes: Airport-side zone; Sharjah International is the UAE's main dedicated air-cargo hub for regional freighters.

zones.name: Ras Al Khaimah Economic Zone (RAKEZ)

location.city: Ras Al Khaimah (Al Hamra / Al Ghail)

zones.incentives: Free-zone and non-free-zone licences, 100% ownership, low-cost industrial land
zones.projects: Saqr 2.0 port-linked free zone (5m m2 phase 1, to 14m m2) by 2027 (RAK Ports)
zones.notes: Formed by merging RAK Free Trade Zone and RAK Investment Authority; Etihad Rail freight terminal at Al Ghayl.

zones.name: Fujairah Free Zone and Fujairah Oil Industry Zone (FOIZ)
zones.authority: Fujairah Free Zone Authority (FFZA); FOIZ Authority (Government of Fujairah)
zones.incentives: Tax-free environment, 100% foreign ownership, direct access to Port of Fujairah oil berths and Habshan–Fujairah pipeline
zones.tenants: FOIZ hosts multiple independent liquid-bulk terminals (Vopak Horizon, ADNOC, etc.), a refinery and processing units; c.18m m3 storage
zones.projects: ADNOC underground crude storage; DP World Al Rugaylat/Dibba terminals adjacent (2026–28)
zones.notes: FOIZ is the Middle East's largest commercial refined-product storage hub; Fujairah is the world's 4th-largest bunkering port (2025).

zones.name: Dubai Airport Free Zone (DAFZA)
zones.authority: Dubai Airport Free Zone Authority (Dubai Integrated Economic Zones Authority)
zones.incentives: 100% foreign ownership, 0% import/export duties, free-zone tax regime, airside access to DXB cargo
zones.tenants: >2,000 registered businesses; c.4.7% of Dubai GDP

corridors.name: Etihad Rail national freight network (Al Ghuweifat – Ruwais – Abu Dhabi – Dubai – Sharjah – Fujairah)
corridors.route: Al Ghuweifat (Saudi border) → Ruwais/Habshan/Shah → ICAD & Khalifa Port (Abu Dhabi) → Dubai Industrial City & Jebel Ali → Sharjah/Al Ghayl (RAK) → Fujairah Port (and Khor Fakkan link agreed 2026)
corridors.length: c.900 km (Stage 1 264 km opened 2016; Stage 2 605 km completed Feb 2023)
corridors.operator: Etihad Rail (federal, Government of Abu Dhabi / UAE)
corridors.capacity_or_traffic: 2025: >10m t aggregates, 6.5m t sulphur, 148,000 containers; aggregate line at 100% capacity (up to 60,000 t/day); target 60m t/year by 2030; each train replaces c.300 trucks
corridors.projects: Aggregate-line capacity expansion (2025); bonded rail corridor Khalifa Port–Fujairah (pilot late 2025); Khor Fakkan connection agreement with Gulftainer (2026); passenger service launched 30 June 2026 (Abu Dhabi–Fujairah); 38 additional locomotives ordered
corridors.notes: Seven freight terminals (Ruwais, ICAD, Khalifa Port, Dubai Industrial City, Jebel Ali Port, Al Ghayl, Fujairah). Became the domestic Hormuz-bypass landbridge in 2026, including the first vehicle train (Nissan cars Fujairah→Abu Dhabi). Serves both DP World (Jebel Ali) and AD Ports (Khalifa) terminals.

corridors.name: DP World east-coast landbridge: Fujairah (Al Rugaylat/Dibba) – Jebel Ali/Jafza
corridors.route: Al Rugaylat & Dibba terminals (Gulf of Oman) → E89/E99 east-coast highways and Etihad Rail Fujairah terminal → Sharjah/Dubai → Jebel Ali Port & Jafza
corridors.operator: DP World (inland logistics network) with Etihad Rail
corridors.capacity_or_traffic: Planned: 2.5m TEU, 1.7m t general cargo, 190,000 CEU at Al Rugaylat; 3.6m t at Dibba; lifts DP World UAE capacity from 19.4m to c.22m TEU
corridors.projects: 50-year concession signed 22 July 2026 with Fujairah Ports Authority; construction 24–30 months (commercial availability c.2028); part of DP World's ~US$3bn 2026 capex
corridors.notes: DP WORLD PROJECT. Strategic response to the 2026 Hormuz closure that cut Jebel Ali volumes 90% in Q2 2026; designed for ULCVs so mainline calls can stay outside Hormuz with cargo trucked/railed to Dubai.

corridors.name: Khor Fakkan – Al Dhaid – Sajaa – Sharjah/Dubai road & rail corridor (Gulftainer)
corridors.route: Khor Fakkan Container Terminal → Sharjah–Khor Fakkan highway (E89 via Al Dhaid) → Al Dhaid dry port → Sajaa dry port → Sharjah/Dubai consumption centres and Jebel Ali
corridors.operator: Gulftainer (terminals, dry ports, GT Maritime feeders); Etihad Rail for rail leg
corridors.capacity_or_traffic: Truck traffic 7,000/day (2026) vs 100 pre-crisis; 65,000 TEU/week through Khor Fakkan (July 2026); planned 2.3m TEU/year inland capacity (Al Dhaid 1.5m TEU + Sajaa)
corridors.projects: US$2bn Gulftainer masterplan (July 2026): Al Dhaid dry port phase 1 (500,000 TEU within 45 days, 1.5m TEU in 6 months), new truck marshalling yard, Khor Fakkan–Etihad Rail connection agreement
corridors.notes: COMPETITOR corridor to DP World's Fujairah landbridge; absorbed the bulk of UAE imports during the Hormuz closure.

corridors.name: Habshan – Fujairah crude oil pipeline (ADCOP)
corridors.route: Habshan (Bab field, Al Dhafra, Abu Dhabi) → Hajar mountains → Fujairah oil terminal / FOIZ
corridors.capacity_or_traffic: 1.5m bpd design capacity; carried the bulk of UAE crude exports (>1.7m bpd crude and products loaded at Fujairah) during the 2026 Hormuz closure
corridors.projects: ADNOC underground crude storage caverns at Fujairah (three crude grades) under construction
corridors.notes: Built 2012 at c.US$4.2bn specifically to bypass Hormuz; Fujairah loadings disrupted by drone strikes 14–15 March 2026.

corridors.name: Hafeet Rail (Etihad Rail – Oman link, Abu Dhabi/Al Ain – Sohar)
corridors.route: Etihad Rail network at Abu Dhabi → Al Ain → Hafeet/Buraimi border → Sohar Port (Oman)
corridors.length: 238 km new line (c.300 km including UAE links)
corridors.operator: Hafeet Rail (JV of Etihad Rail, Oman Rail/Asyad Group and Mubadala)
corridors.capacity_or_traffic: Planned freight trains >15,000 t (c.270 containers) per journey; passenger up to 200 km/h
corridors.projects: AED 5.5bn (US$1.5bn) civil-works contracts awarded April 2024; construction 50–70% complete (Oct 2025); testing/commissioning from early 2026; first cross-border link of the GCC Railway
corridors.notes: Would give Abu Dhabi/KEZAD and Dubai a rail outlet to Sohar outside Hormuz, complementing the Fujairah/Khor Fakkan routes; Sohar was named primary gateway of the Dubai–Oman green corridor (Mar 2026).

corridors.name: Dubai – Oman 'Green Corridor' road route (Sohar – Al Wajajah/Hatta – Dubai)
corridors.route: Sohar Port (also Salalah, Duqm) → Oman Route 7 → Al Wajajah (OM) / Hatta (AE) → E44 Hatta–Dubai road → Jebel Ali, Dubai airports, local market
corridors.operator: Dubai Customs and Oman customs (Dubai Customs Notice 04/2026); commercial truckers
corridors.capacity_or_traffic: Transit planning: Oman clearance same day–48 h, road leg several hours, Hatta to final destination same day; Hatta crossing 3,500–4,500 crossings/day (all traffic); Hatta trade 'rises sharply' in 2026 (AGBI, Sep 2026)
corridors.projects: Green corridor launched 13–14 March 2026 for sealed containers bound for Jebel Ali/Dubai and re-exports via Omani ports; bidirectional
corridors.notes: Created within weeks of the Hormuz closure; carriers (e.g. ONE) redirected empties to Sohar. Alternative road corridors via Khatmat Malaha (Sohar–Fujairah/Kalba) and Mezyad (Al Ain).

corridors.name: UAE – Saudi Arabia road corridor (Abu Dhabi – Al Ghuweifat/Al Batha – Riyadh/Dammam)
corridors.route: Jebel Ali/Dubai → E11 Sheikh Zayed Rd → Abu Dhabi → E11 Al Dhafra → Al Ghuweifat (AE) / Al Batha (SA) → Saudi Highway 95/10 → Riyadh, Dammam, Jeddah
corridors.length: c.370 km Dubai–Ghuweifat; c.900 km Dubai–Riyadh
corridors.operator: Federal/Emirate road authorities; Etihad Rail line to Ghuweifat parallels it (future GCC Railway link to Saudi)
corridors.capacity_or_traffic: Bilateral trade >US$20bn/year; truck volumes elevated in 2026 as Hormuz closure pushed cargo to road; delays of hours to more than a week reported June–Aug 2026
corridors.projects: GCC Railway Saudi–UAE link via Ghuweifat (Etihad Rail track already reaches the border; Saudi side not built)
corridors.notes: Land route used for Europe–Gulf overland trucking during the crisis (e.g. Spinneys 16-day Kent–Dubai run). Saudi–UAE political tensions in 2026 added unexplained holds at Al Batha.

border_crossings.name: Al Ghuweifat (UAE) / Al Batha (Saudi Arabia)
border_crossings.traffic: The UAE's only land crossing with Saudi Arabia and the main truck gateway for Gulf land trade (>US$20bn bilateral trade/year); truck queues historically up to 22 km; volumes elevated summer 2026
border_crossings.projects: Etihad Rail freight line terminates at Ghuweifat awaiting Saudi-side GCC Railway connection; past clearance-acceleration measures at Al Ghuwaifat post
border_crossings.notes: June–Aug 2026: waits from hours to more than a week, goods 'held up without explanation' amid Saudi–UAE tensions and Hormuz-driven road surge; Saudi customs deny systematic delays.

border_crossings.name: Hatta (UAE) / Al Wajajah (Oman)
border_crossings.traffic: 3,500–4,500 crossings/day (all traffic); primary Dubai–Muscat/Sohar truck route; trade through Hatta 'rises sharply' in 2026
border_crossings.projects: Dubai–Oman green corridor for sealed containers (Dubai Customs Notice 04/2026, March 2026)
border_crossings.notes: Typical wait 30–60 min, 3–4 h at peaks; became the key Hormuz-bypass road gateway from Sohar into Dubai in 2026.

border_crossings.name: Khatmat Malaha (Oman) / Kalba–Wadi Al Helo (UAE)
border_crossings.traffic: Handles vehicles and commercial trucks; shortest link between Sohar and Fujairah/Khor Fakkan/Kalba; volumes n/a
border_crossings.notes: East-coast alternative to Hatta for Sohar–Fujairah traffic; c.25 km from the Hatta crossing per border guides.

border_crossings.name: Mezyad (UAE) / Hafeet (Oman)
border_crossings.traffic: Main Abu Dhabi/Al Ain–Buraimi–Ibri–Nizwa/Muscat road crossing; volumes n/a
border_crossings.projects: Hafeet Rail (238 km Abu Dhabi–Al Ain–Sohar) crosses the border near here; construction 50–70% complete Oct 2025, commissioning from 2026
border_crossings.notes: Historic Buraimi oasis crossing; passport controls imposed since Nov 2006. Future road+rail gateway once Hafeet Rail opens.

border_crossings.name: Al Dara (Ras Al Khaimah) / Tibat (Oman, Musandam)
border_crossings.traffic: Only road access to Musandam (Khasab); light commercial and passenger traffic; volumes n/a
border_crossings.notes: Minor freight relevance; Musandam is supplied largely via this crossing and by sea from Khasab. Detail not confirmed in accessed sources beyond general border guides.

border_crossings.name: Dibba Al Fujairah / Dibba Al Hisn (UAE) – Dibba Al Baya (Oman, Musandam)
border_crossings.traffic: Local passenger and light goods traffic to Dibba Al Baya; not a trucking gateway; volumes n/a
border_crossings.projects: DP World Dibba general-cargo terminal (3.6m t/year) under 50-year concession signed July 2026, adjacent to the border town
border_crossings.notes: Freight relevance is the new DP World Dibba terminal rather than the crossing itself.
